classification.difficultyReason: Follow and justify a two-tower construction, then reproduce the result using the requested alternate sine-rule route.

content.prompt:
Two towers $AB$ and $PQ$ stand on level ground. Tower $AB$ is 12 metres taller than tower $PQ$.
From $A$, the angles of depression of $P$ and $Q$ are $28°$ and $64°$ respectively.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 16 tower diagram beneath part d
spec.description: Schematic taller tower AB on the left and shorter PQ on the right. Horizontal KP and ground BQ, descending AP and AQ, dashed horizontal from A. AK has a left-side 12 m label. Right-angle squares at K, B and Q. Cyan depression sector at A, external curved leader for 64°, and 28° below the dashed horizontal.
spec.mathematics: AK=12 m; BKPQ is a rectangle. Depression from the horizontal at A to AP is 28° and to AQ is 64°. Source diagram is schematic, with no additional numerical labels.

answer.worked:
$\angle KAP=90°-28°=62°$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan62°&=\frac{KP}{12}\\[8pt]KP&=12\tan62°.\end{align*}$$
Opposite sides of rectangle $BKPQ$ are equal, so $BQ=KP=12\tan62°$.

$\angle AQB=64°$ by alternate angles between parallel horizontal lines.
$$\begin{align*}\tan64°&=\frac{AB}{BQ}\\[8pt]AB&=BQ\tan64°\\AB&=12\tan62°\tan64°.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence find the height of the shorter tower, correct to the nearest metre.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Solve the problem again by using $\triangle AKP$ to find $AP$, and then using the sine rule in $\triangle APQ$.

answer.worked:
In right-angled $\triangle AKP$,
$$\begin{align*}\cos62°&=\frac{12}{AP}\\[8pt]AP&=\frac{12}{\cos62°}=\frac{12}{\sin28°}.\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle APQ$, $\angle PAQ=64°-28°=36°$ and $\angle AQP=90°-64°=26°$. By the sine rule,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{PQ}{\sin36°}&=\frac{AP}{\sin26°}\\[8pt]PQ&=\frac{12\sin36°}{\sin28°\sin26°}\\[8pt]PQ&\approx34\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
